title: TokenCraft: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Rate Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Rate Board
options.lineage: bureau-de-change rate boards and bank FX displays
options.thesis: One prompt, converted into what it costs on every model, at live rates.
options.viewport: Prompt on the left with token boundaries drawn on the text itself; on the right a display-size token count, fit bar and a live mini rate board of your cheapest models.
options.risk: Split-flap motion turns gimmicky if it fires on every keystroke; it must roll once per settled change.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale alone: the token count is set at display size, replacing four equal stat tiles.
Every board row carries a cost bar on one fixed log ramp, so cheap and costly read at a glance.
Every model row keeps the same fixed furniture: provider, context, cache tier, exact or estimate.
Context fit is two sides, your input and reserved output, against a hard capacity with totals right-aligned.
Token boundaries sit on a strict monospace cell grid, so splits line up and scan.

options.label: The Type Case
options.lineage: letterpress composing sticks and type cases
options.thesis: Tokenizing is typesetting: your text set as sorts pulled from a 200k-piece case.
options.viewport: A composing stick runs across the top holding your prompt as sorts, each stamped with its token ID; the proof below carries count and cost.
options.risk: Letterpress is a familiar craft trope and can read as costume on a fast working tool.

options.label: Dark-first Console
options.lineage: digital design canon: dark developer consoles
options.thesis: Graphite panels, hairline seams, syntax colours only for state.
options.viewport: Tiled persistent panels: editor, token stream, cost table, with a command bar.
options.case: Developers identify instantly; loses on clarity because it is what TokenCraft already looks like.
options.risk: Close to the current site and to every competitor; distinction would rest on details alone.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: A giant number that breathes as you type.
options.viewport: One enormous token count, tiny mono labels.
options.case: Developers don't identify with a type foundry; the multi-model job disappears.
options.risk: Pretty, but it hides the cost job.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale alone: the count goes to display size.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: 95 models as stars, cost as magnitude.
options.viewport: A sky chart of models plotted by price and context.
options.case: A chart nobody asked for; reading a price takes longer than in a table.
options.risk: Looks like norai.tech's starfield hero, blurring the family line.
options.kept: One fixed log ramp for cost bars on every row.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Models as a ranked mascot roster.
options.kept: Fixed furniture on every model row.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: Your context window is a tape that must not overflow.
options.viewport: Side A input, side B output, running times right-aligned.
options.case: Lovely fit metaphor but nostalgia over clarity.
options.kept: Input and reserved output as two sides against one capacity.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Text built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Prompt glyphs on a visible construction grid.
options.kept: Token boundaries on a strict mono cell grid.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: tiktokenizer-style two panes: text left, coloured token chips right, count on top.
canonCard.viewport: Model select, textarea, chip stream, a count badge.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
